description: Somos 404:FNF, un equipo de ingeniería participando en modalidad virtual dentro de la sede de Lima. Resolveremos el desafío "Flame in Freefall", desarrollando una plataforma impulsada por inteligencia artificial y modelos de pronóstico para analizar datos de combustión en microgravedad. Buscamos habilidades en análisis de datos, machine learning y visualización para colaborar en remoto.
summary: 404:FNF is a web-based data analysis and synthesis platform developed to organize, classify, and interpret microgravity combustion datasets from the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository. In microgravity, the absence of buoyant convection alters flame geometry, soot and aerosol coagulation, and extinction limits, making normal-gravity flammability tests insufficient for spacecraft fire safety design. Because raw PSI investigations contain hundreds of gigabytes of heterogeneous files and uncompressed video, comparing experimental conditions across studies is difficult. Our platform normalizes and links experimental tables and metadata from PSI combustion investigations across NASA's three fire safety pillars: prevention, detection, and suppression. It allows students, researchers, and engineers to evaluate which experimental evidence applies to specific habitable environments (such as the ISS, lunar surface habitats, pressurized rovers, and spacesuits), perform regression and flammability analyses within valid physical domains, and identify experimental gaps for future space missions
details:
404:FNF is an interactive web platform designed to consult, compare, and analyze microgravity combustion research from the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database for human spaceflight fire safety. Rather than acting as an unverified black-box predictor, the platform prioritizes data traceability, experimental context, and physical validity. It organizes the scientific evidence into three core areas:

  1. Prevention: Analyzes solid and gaseous material flammability using data from BASS, BASS-II, SAFFIRE-I, SAFFIRE-II, SAFFIRE-III, ACME BRE, ACME CFI-G, SLICE, and SPICE. It examines how oxygen concentration, ambient pressure, fuel geometry, and low-velocity ventilation airflows govern flame spread in microgravity compared to terrestrial standards such as NASA-STD-6001 Test 1.
  2. Detection: Synthesizes smoke aerosol measurements from SAME and SAME-R alongside hardware feasibility tests from DAFT and DAFT-2, where commercial TSI P-Trak condensation nucleus counters were modified with capillary condenser tubes to operate in low gravity. This section summarizes how particle size distributions, aging, and ventilation affect photoelectric and ionization smoke detectors.
  3. Suppression: Examines liquid droplet combustion, Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) boundaries, gaseous suppressants (CO2 and He), low-temperature cool-flame transitions, flow-reduction extinctions, and electric-field flame control using data from FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI, BASS-II, and ACME E-FIELD Flames.

How it works: We developed a data normalization and verification pipeline in Python and JavaScript that processes experimental CSV tables, ISA-Tab metadata files (.txt), and technical documentation from the PSI repository (compiling 2,009 total records across the studied investigations). The pipeline separates 1,871 individual experimental tests from test-day summaries, campaign summaries, pre-test visualizations, and documentary notes so that aggregate records do not bias statistical counts or plots. It also preserves measurement qualifiers (exact values, approximate values, censored bounds such as < or >, and intervals), tracks pressure provenance (measured, assumed from cabin baselines, or unreported), retains signed airflow conventions, and evaluates data quality per variable rather than discarding entire rows for single-sensor anomalies.

On top of this normalized dataset, the web application allows users to select mission scenarios (Earth, ISS, nominal spacecraft, EVA preparation, spacesuits, lunar base, pressurized rover, and Mars) based on oxygen concentration, total and partial pressure, and gravity level. Users can filter and rank investigations by experimental compatibility and mission relevance, compare studies side by side, run statistical regression and predictive models that explicitly distinguish between model fit, cross-validation, and out-of-domain extrapolation, and consult an SI-assisted query tool grounded in the PSI documentation with DOI and PSI-ID citations.

Benefits and goals: Our objective is to provide an accessible, rigorous reference tool for undergraduate and graduate students, professors, researchers, and aerospace engineers. The platform makes it possible to inspect PSI combustion data without downloading hundreds of gigabytes of raw video files, clarifies which experimental results can be interpolated or bounded between 0g and 1g, highlights where partial-gravity data are currently missing ahead of future lunar experiments (such as LUCI, FM2, and SoFIE), and connects spaceflight findings to terrestrial applications including fine-water-mist extinguishers, smoke detector calibration, and firefighter protective equipment.

Tools, coding languages, and software used: Python 3 (pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, FastAPI, pytest) for data harvesting, normalization, statistical modeling, and automated testing; JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, and CSS3 for the web interface and data visualizations; Git and GitHub for version control and deployment
dataRefs: Our project processes, normalizes, and links experimental CSV tables, ISA-Tab metadata files (.txt), and technical reports from the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository, along with NASA flammability standards and challenge documentation: PSI-69: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX, DOI: 10.60555/mbq8-0451) - Experimental table (275 total records; 258 valid droplet combustion tests for Methanol and Heptane), ISA-Tab metadata, and engineering requirements documents. PSI-68: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2 (FLEX-2) - Experimental table and metadata for droplet combustion, convective flows, and cool-flame transitions. PSI-39: Cool Flames Investigation (CFI) - Experimental records for alkane droplet combustion and low-temperature chemistry in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR). PSI-26: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS) - Experimental table and metadata for solid fuel flammability and airflow effects in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG). PSI-25: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II) - Experimental table, initial and final calibrated oxygen records, flow-reduction extinctions, and PMMA rod flammability boundary data. PSI-98, PSI-99, and PSI-100: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiments I, II, and III (SAFFIRE-I, SAFFIRE-II, SAFFIRE-III) - Large-scale microgravity flame spread and flammability limit records aboard the Cygnus spacecraft. PSI-102 and PSI-101: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME and SAME-R) - Metadata and experimental tables on smoke particle size distributions, aging, Pyrell intumescent samples, and smoke detector responses. PSI-47: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test (DAFT / DAFT-2) - Experimental table and metadata on capillary-modified TSI P-Trak condensation nucleus counters in microgravity. PSI-159: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (ACME CFI-G) - Experimental tables for normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames with oxygen concentrations up to 85% O2. PSI-20: ACME Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) - Experimental table and metadata for gaseous emulation of condensed-phase material flammability. PSI-22: ACME Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (E-FIELD Flames) - Experimental table and metadata on ion-driven convection under electric fields, used to study flame suppression and partial-gravity simulation. PSI-10: ACME Flame Design - Spherical diffusion flame soot inception and radiative extinction data. PSI-106: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment (SLICE) - Experimental table and metadata on co-flow laminar diffusion flame structure and liftoff stability. PSI-107: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment (SPICE) - Experimental table and metadata on microgravity co-flow flame smoke points and soot onset. NASA Technical Standard NASA-STD-6001 (Flammability, Offgassing, and Compatibility Requirements and Test Procedures) and NASA 2026 Challenge background materials on future partial-gravity experiments (LUCI, FM2, and SoFIE).
